title: Fast sleep: learning new rules quickly from few examples and little compute

brief.state:
Fast sleep = learn a new C2 rule overnight so the first try is right next time, on B2 (3.3M params). Files read through the 2:48 PM ET progress board, 2026-10-07. No sealed test file was opened.

Shown on DEV (6 confirm parents unless noted): the memory sleep ("M", a kNN notebook of the night's correct programs plus 512 old add/mult notes, no weight change) costs 0.78-1.16 TFLOP against 19-39 for the fine-tune. It reaches 0.87x the fine-tune's gain (+32.1 vs +37.0) and failed its harm mark (3.9 points on s205, caused by the answer note). The answer note is now off, a post-hoc choice (suggested). A fresh harm check with it off passed on 8 parents. The answer note behind an agreement gate gained +0.98 against a +1.0 bar, so it is not adopted. Night chaining into the notebook is proved wrong (+0.7 against +5). Fine-tuning on chained search records partly learns x^2+k (sq_plus 0-2% to 20-27%) but not a*x+b (2-4%), on 2 parents. Affine stays at 0-4% in every arm, including a sleep on correct programs.

The real C2b (job 9: arms W, R, H, M on six parents) started on the Mac at 4:36 AM ET. The sealed test is scored once after training.

Two things the orchestrator summary leaves out. First, the progress board reports 72.7% on a holdout (2 seeds) from a research loop, but that loop is under audit because its replay range was hand-picked, and no results file backs it. Second, Ben's 2:45 PM ET key rule says the deployed model must do everything itself, and hand code may run only as a tool the model calls. The notebook's lookup, its fixed gate (0.99 quantile, floor 0.9) and its c=50 vote boost run inside every forward pass. The stepping stones for held-out kinds are hand-written, and the fast-sleep parents skip the add/mult replay that C2b's N' has. So no harm check exists on N'.

area_summary:
94 raw ideas merged into 28 distinct, 13 ids dropped. Three corrections change how this area should be read.

(1) The research loop has a results file: a compliant 6-seed holdout of 71.3 +/- 2.5 (sq_plus 76.6, double_add 72.5, affine 15.5) at about 2,400 TF per sleep, with no notebook. The 72.7 figure is the non-compliant segment 1. The holdout is 'same rules, new questions', so it cannot tell memorising the 65 usable programs from learning a rule. A copy-only notebook is capped near 63% pooled, so the notebook branch cannot meet 70% alone.

(2) No file backs '10,000 TF in 5 hours'. Cloud CPU gives 850-1,300 TF per 5 h, but the Mac's job-8 wall-clock implies about 0.16 TF/s (about 2,900 TF), which would fit the 2,400 TF night in about 4 hours (suggested, one timing script to confirm).
